title: The Traveler and the Mystery of Providence
summary: A wise traveler was resting beneath the shade of an ancient oak tree beside a bubbling mountain spring. As he watched, a wealthy horseman arrived, dismounted to drink, and rode ...
keywords: the prophet and the justice of providence
full_text:
A wise traveler was resting beneath the shade of an ancient oak tree beside a bubbling mountain spring. As he watched, a wealthy horseman arrived, dismounted to drink, and rode away, accidentally leaving behind a heavy leather pouch of gold coins upon the moss.

Shortly after, a poor boy arrived with a flock of sheep, found the purse of gold, rejoiced with pure innocence, and took it home to buy bread for his starving mother.

Next, an old woodcutter, weary and bent under a heavy load of firewood, sat down by the spring to rest his aching limbs.

Suddenly, the horseman galloped back, searching frantically for his lost gold. Finding the old woodcutter sitting alone by the spring, the horseman accused him of theft, beat the innocent old man with his crop, and rode away in fury when no gold was found.

The traveler was deeply troubled by what he had witnessed, crying out: 'Where is the justice of this world? The wealthy man lost his coin; the boy took what was not his; and the innocent old woodcutter was beaten for a deed he never committed!'

At that moment, a gentle celestial messenger appeared beside the spring and revealed the hidden threads of destiny:

'Judge not with superficial eyes, O traveler! Know that the horseman had stolen those exact gold coins from the boy’s father twenty years ago; the gold was merely restored to its rightful heir. And know that the old woodcutter had in his youth struck down the horseman’s brother in an unpunished brawl; today, his past debt was expiated without his life being taken! Every deed in the universe is weighed with absolute precision by a balance that human eyes cannot fathom.'

The traveler bowed his head in profound humility, learning that patience and faith must trust the deeper justice that governs the world.
moral: Human judgment sees only the surface of events; divine providence guides all things with profound hidden justice.
